key_insight: Integrating standardized trial data with biomedical ontologies improved vaccine trial retrieval and adverse-event ranking; this study concerns vaccine trial analytics, not AI cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support cross-trial vaccine research and study planning, but does not establish clinical benefit or validate treatment decisions.
method: Mapped 9,147 vaccine-related AACT records into the Study-Experiment-Assay Common Data Model.
Linked vaccine products and reported adverse events to VO and OAE ontologies in relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph.
Evaluated semantic retrieval, adverse-event ranking, trial similarity, and machine-learning-based design recommendations.
evidence_signal: Ontology-expanded queries retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials versus 16 with exact identifier matching, while context-aware adverse-event ranking improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383.
watch_item: Design recommendation performance varied across 23 vaccine classes under leave-one-Material-out evaluation, limiting claims of broad generalizability.
paper_title: Ontology-Based SEA-CDM Integration for Vaccine Clinical Trials: Query, Similarity, and Design Recommendation
